substrands.name: Speaking: Etiquette and Pronunciation

values: Love: The learner portrays a caring attitude as they interrupt and disagree politely in a debate about careers.

assessment_rubric.below: Pick out information from atlases, manuals, newspapers and encyclopedias for general knowledge but leaves out most details

assessment_rubric.indicator: Ability to rewrite comma splices, run on sentences and run on lines as complete sentences
assessment_rubric.exceeds: Rewrites comma splices, run on sentences and run on lines as complete sentences with consistency
assessment_rubric.meets: Rewrites comma splices, run on sentences and run on lines as complete sentences
assessment_rubric.approaches: Rewrites comma splices, run on sentences and run on lines as complete sentences in most cases
assessment_rubric.below: Rewrites comma splices, run on sentences and run on lines as complete sentences but with assistance

assessment_rubric.indicator: Ability to order ideas in a paragraph for coherence
assessment_rubric.exceeds: Orders ideas in a paragraph for coherence in a variety of contexts
assessment_rubric.meets: Orders ideas in a paragraph for coherence
assessment_rubric.approaches: Partially orders ideas in a paragraph for coherence
assessment_rubric.below: Orders ideas in a paragraph for coherence when prompted

assessment_rubric.indicator: Ability to write a descriptive narrative essay on a given topic

assessment_rubric.meets: Writes a descriptive narrative essay on a given topic
assessment_rubric.approaches: Writes a flat and colourless descriptive narrative essay on a given topic
assessment_rubric.below: Write a descriptive narrative essay on given topics with a lot of assistance

substrands.name: Speaking: Etiquette
learning_outcomes: pick out the target sounds and aspects of etiquette in oral or written texts
use appropriate etiquette in different contexts
articulate the sounds /ɒ/ and /ɔ: / for effective communication
justify the need for accurate pronunciation in communication.
learning_experiences: listen to an oral passage and identify the words with the sounds /ɒ/ and /ɔ: /
say tongue twisters which have the target sound with peers
present minimal pairs featuring the target sounds and receive peer review
watch videos depicting the use of etiquette in the following instances: o hotels o telephone conversation o the market among others
pick out the polite words and phrases used in the video and list them
conduct a telephone conversation and observe etiquette
role play a conversation between a receptionist and a guest, a secretary and a parent in a school or a customer and a seller in a market.
inquiry_questions: Why is it important to observe etiquette?
core_competencies: Critical thinking and problem solving: The learner seeks clarifications as they outline different contexts where business and market place etiquette is applicable. Creativity: The learner undertakes group tasks and gains a new perspective as role play a conversation between a receptionist and a guest, a secretary and a parent in a school or a customer and a seller in a market.
values: Respect: The learner understands and appreciates others as they present minimal pairs featuring the target sounds and receive peer review. Unity: The learner displays team spirit when they jointly practise correct articulation of sounds.
pertinent_issues: Socio-economic issues: The learners promote social etiquette as they list conventions observed in the video on business and market etiquette.

substrands.name: Critical Listening
learning_outcomes: describe various forms of distractions to effective listening in different contexts
determine the speaker, context and intention in varied oral texts
select key points from an audio text for information
appreciate the importance of critical listening in communication.
learning_experiences: brainstorm on different forms of distractions and how to avoid them
collaboratively search for information online and offline on how to identify the speaker, context and intention
listen to a variety of audio texts and identify the speaker, context and intention
listen to a variety of texts on the theme while avoiding distractions
pick out the key points from an audio text and make notes.
inquiry_questions: 1. How can we ensure we gain the most out of a listening text?
2. Why is it important to listen to key points in a text?
core_competencies: Core competencies to be developed:
Creativity and imagination: The learner will generate new ideas as they brainstorm on different forms of distractions and how to avoid them.
Communication and collaboration: The learner will listen critically and show awareness of the speaker, context and intention in varied oral texts. Values:
Responsibility: The learners engage in assigned duties and roles as they collaboratively search for information online and offline on how to identify the speaker, context and intention.

Love: The learner portrays a caring attitude as they brainstorm different forms of distractions and how to avoid them. Pertinent and Contemporary Issues (PCIs) Environmental conservation: The learner’s awareness on climate change is heightened as they listen to texts on the theme and pick out main points.

substrands.name: Conversational skills

articulate the sounds / ə /, /ɑ: / and / ɜ: / for oral fluency
use discourse markers to organise ideas during conversations
apply onomatopoeic words and idiophones in oral communication
advocate the need to organise ideas appropriately in oral communication.
learning_experiences: collaboratively recite poems or form minimal pairs with the sounds / ə /, /ɑ: / and / ɜ: /

select and group words from newspapers, magazines, online texts, radio programmes, news bulletins, television shows among others, which: o start a conversation (Right, Now...) o end a conversation (so, okay, anyway...)
o change and manage a topic (Did you try, Did you, Incidentally, By the way, Speaking of...) o order what we say (and, first, second, for a start, next...)
watch a video and note how speakers start, end or change a topic during a conversation
role play a conversation using transitional words (discourse markers/linking words) on conversational cards
collaboratively practise changing a topic and
ordering ideas during mock speeches
identify onomatopoeic words and idiophones in an oral text
use onomatopoeic words and idiophones in a story telling session.
inquiry_questions: 1. Why does the proper articulation of sounds matter?
2. How do discourse markers affect the flow of conversations?
core_competencies: Learning to learn: The learner carries out research as they look for examples of discourse markers in books or the internet.
Self-efficacy: The learner displays attention to detail as they watch a video and note how speakers start, end or change a topic during a conversation.
values: Patriotism: The learners exercise dedication when they collaboratively practise changing a topic and ordering ideas during mock speeches.
Unity: The learner avoids discrimination as they collaboratively recite poems or form minimal pairs with the sounds / ə /, /ɑ: / and / ɜ: /.
pertinent_issues: Pertinent and Contemporary Issues (PCIs): Socio-economic and environmental issues: The learners engage in peaceful conflict management as they use fillers and discourse markers to recount events in a story on the environment.

substrands.name: Intensive Listening
learning_outcomes: select specific details from a listening text
use words and phrases picked from an oral text in a variety of contexts
advocate the need to discriminate among sounds for effective communication.
learning_experiences: listen to an audio recording and focus on key words, dates, names, important facts and phrases, similes and metaphors as well as words with the sounds /ᴧ / / æ / / aʊ / /əʊ/ /w/ /j/
play language games using the target sounds, key words, dates, names, important facts and phrases
practise listening to a text with a partner and ask them to speak slowly and clearly
take notes while listening to the partner
collaboratively engage in a cloze test using the words and phrases identified.
inquiry_questions: 1. How do we pick out specific details from a listening text?
2. Why is it important to focus on specific details in a listening text?
core_competencies: Core competencies to be developed:
Learning to learn: The learners seek advice as they take notes while listening to the partner.

Critical thinking: The learners follow instructions as they work collaboratively with peers to play language games using the target sounds, key words, dates, names, important facts and phrases. Values:
Responsibility: The learner’s resilience is enhanced as they play language games using the target sounds, key words, dates, names, important facts and phrases.

Peace: The learner displays tolerance as they practise listening to a text with a partner and ask them to speak slowly and clearly. Pertinent and Contemporary Issues (PCIs): Citizenship education- Peace education: The learners respect each other’s diversity as they practise listening to a text with a partner and ask them to speak slowly and clearly.

substrands.name: Nonverbal Cues

values: Respect: The learner appreciates diverse opinions as they watch video clips and identify nonverbal cues such as dress choice, personal space and body movement among others.
